label: late original-phase j/t/s/z/k input in sequences starting with f/0/o/q/d/a
explanation: Fires almost only during the original (input) phase (99.9% of mass), at positions t>=3 (it never fires at t=0-1 and barely at t=2); the rate peaks at orig_idx 5-6 and near the end of the input (to_go 0-2). It looks like a conjunction of two factors: the current input is one of j, t, s, z, k (lift 3-5x; weaker for 1, m, r), and the sequence starts with f, 0, o, q, d or a (first_tok lift 2.5-6x, strongest for f). Having more of those tokens among the first few positions also raises activation. It is mostly the first occurrence of the input token (in_first=1 carries 92% of mass). It is essentially silent at the delimiter and during the copy phase. The top activations (~0.21-0.22) are j/t/s/z inputs at t=5-7 in sequences that begin with runs like f f, 0 f f, o q q. The conjunction gets dev F1 ~0.49 (precision 0.52, recall 0.46, mass recall 0.58), and covers more of the top quartile (0.69) than of the bottom. The response looks graded and additive across token identities rather than a crisp rule, so many weaker activations fall on other tokens or other first tokens.
